From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>

Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@asterpay.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit: sprint uplift, tier rebid & lifecycle plan

Hi Elaine / Daniel —

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. Per our notes, AsterPay is seeing a predictable uplift in peak checkout volume and the current hosted tier is hitting the soft-throttle window more frequently. I pulled the last 6 months of usage and attached a short CSV with daily peak tokens for your review.

High-level proposal:
- Move from current monthly commit of 1.2B tokens to a stepped commit that starts at 2.2B/mo for the next 3 months, then transitions to 3.5B/mo on month 4.
- Add a burst pocket (100M tokens/mo) for seasonal spikes, billed only when used.
- Keep the same per-token unit price for the committed volume; incremental overage rate set at a reduced uplift versus on-demand.
- Soft-throttle policy: extend the soft-throttle grace to 120s at 95th percentile peak to avoid user-facing failures while autoscaling warms GPUs.

If this looks reasonable I can circulate a formal updated proposal (Commit_Proposal_v2.pdf) and ask Finance to prepare the PR. Two asks from your side: confirm expected seasonality window (June–Aug) and any procurement timing constraints.

Attaching: AsterPay_MonthlyUsage.csv (summary), initial draft proposal.

Thanks —
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0186

Rohan —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick notes from product + ops:

- The burst pocket is appealing; would you remind me how the burst billing shows on the monthly invoice (line item or blended)?
- Procurement: we need PO terms by 10 May to hit our vendor cutover calendar.

Can you also confirm SLO implications if we keep the current model but increase the per-second ingestion cap? We want to avoid double-paying for reserved capacity and burst.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API commit: sprint uplift, tier rebid & lifecycle plan — pricing + SLO check

Thanks for the context. Quick technical/pricing responses below:

1) Pricing model: the stepped commit proposal is fine from pricing; we recommend this language on the invoice:
   - Committed volume (stepped): 2.2B tokens @ $0.0009/token (months 1–3); 3.5B tokens @ $0.00085/token (month 4 onward)
   - Burst pocket: 100M tokens at $0.00125/token when used (appears as a separate line item "Burst usage")
   - Overage beyond commit + burst billed at $0.0018/token

   We can provide a blended billing view on request, but by default burst shows as its own line item — easier for AsterPay finance to reconcile.

2) Ingestion cap / SLO: we can bump the per-second ingestion cap for the committed pool for June–Aug with the following guardrails:
   - Temporary cap increase to +40% peak QPS for the committed pool (applies only to committed capacity)
   - Soft-throttle extension to 120s at 95th percentile (as proposed) to reduce tail errors while autoscaling fills instances
   - Automatic fallback: if sustained >150% of committed pool for 30m, requests will route to on-demand fallback model (higher cost) with a graceful 5% sampling for latency-sensitive requests to preserve UX

3) Billing double-pay guidance: to avoid double-paying, we propose:
   - Bursts billed only on actual usage and not pre-provisioned.
   - Temporary ingestion cap increases do not create a separate reserved SKU — they apply to the committed pool and are included in committed pricing; only true overage is billed as burst/overage.

I can draft the exact contract language for the PR if we want to lock this in.

—Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
